input.summary:
parts/room-10.mjs (P1 living room) no longer writes its furniture: all 17 writes were refused because shell west owns every cell of the room's interior as air. make.sh now exits 0 with no REFUSED and no off-palette blocks, and build.nbt is written.
The living room is an empty room. The furniture rows and legends are kept in the file for when the lock allows writes.
The fix belongs upstream: shell west should leave the interior unowned (or runParts should lock only non-air cells), and room-10 then calls its three layers() again.
left: The P1 living room has no furniture: sofa, coffee and side tables, rug, barrel shelf and lanterns are all unplaced. Every one of the 17 writes is locked.

Root cause is outside this part: shell-west.mjs writes air over the whole room volume (x19..21, y2..4, z14..20), and build.mjs's runParts locks air-written cells (its own comment says 'air included, so no carving'). The plan's INTERIOR rule says room designers furnish the interior, so the shell's air and the lock contradict each other. This affects every room part that furnishes, not only room-10.

To restore the furniture: have shell-west leave interior cells unwritten (or have runParts lock only solid cells), then restore the three layers() calls in build() (floor y2, tops y3, lanterns y4). The rows and legends are still in parts/room-10.mjs. Check the palette after that, because the report only checks placed blocks.
The report's refusedAt is capped at 8 entries, so the other 9 refused cells were not visible from the log.

waste.what: Worked out which earlier part owns each room cell by dumping MCD_PARTS_CELLS and writing an ad-hoc ASCII map of the room's columns, in order to find out why every write was refused.
waste.cost: ~4 tool calls, one probe script in /tmp, one full build run for the cell dump
waste.tool: A report field per refused write giving the owning part and its block (for example owner 'shell west (plots 0-3)' 'air'), and a runParts summary that flags a part whose whole box is owned by air, so the lock conflict shows up in one line rather than a dump.

waste.what: Checked each block id in the removed writes against palette.json by hand, because the palette report only counts blocks that were placed, so refused writes were never palette-checked.
waste.tool: runParts palette check that also covers refused writes, or a `mcd palette-check <part.mjs>` that lists every id a part names against palette.json.

waste.what: refusedAt is capped at 8 entries, so the log showed only 8 of the 17 refused cells.
waste.cost: a second look at the part file to confirm all 17 were refused (the count matched the layer rows)
waste.tool: Drop the slice(0, 8) cap or print the full list in the part log line when a part is fully refused.

companions.task: Decide the trade order so the shell leaves the room interiors open for the furnishers: the shell-west owner should stop writing air over the rooms, or runParts should lock only solid cells. Then the room-10 layers can be restored.
Fit the sofa, the coffee and side tables, the barrel shelf and the lanterns from the rows already in room-10.mjs once their cells are open, and check the sofa faces the hall opening.

structured_output.summary:
parts/room-10.mjs (P1 living room) no longer writes its furniture: all 17 writes were refused because shell west owns every cell of the room's interior as air. make.sh now exits 0 with no REFUSED and no off-palette blocks, and build.nbt is written.
The living room is an empty room. The furniture rows and legends are kept in the file for when the lock allows writes.
The fix belongs upstream: shell west should leave the interior unowned (or runParts should lock only non-air cells), and room-10 then calls its three layers() again.
left: The P1 living room has no furniture: sofa, coffee and side tables, rug, barrel shelf and lanterns are all unplaced. Every one of the 17 writes is locked.

Root cause is outside this part: shell-west.mjs writes air over the whole room volume (x19..21, y2..4, z14..20), and build.mjs's runParts locks air-written cells (its own comment says 'air included, so no carving'). The plan's INTERIOR rule says room designers furnish the interior, so the shell's air and the lock contradict each other. This affects every room part that furnishes, not only room-10.

To restore the furniture: have shell-west leave interior cells unwritten (or have runParts lock only solid cells), then restore the three layers() calls in build() (floor y2, tops y3, lanterns y4). The rows and legends are still in parts/room-10.mjs. Check the palette after that, because the report only checks placed blocks.
The report's refusedAt is capped at 8 entries, so the other 9 refused cells were not visible from the log.
